zones.what: Lifeboats mounted at Deck 5 obstruct the downward view from balconies on Decks 6-8, with Deck 6 most affected and obstruction lessening on higher decks; horizon view remains clear.
zones.effect: You see the lifeboat tops when looking down but have unobstructed ocean views at eye level and above; the boats are simply part of the foreground.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to those who want to watch the water directly below or photograph straight down; doesn't matter to those focused on horizon views, sunsets, or port scenery.

zones.what: Mid-ship balconies on Decks 7-8 extend past the hull line where the superstructure cantilevers over the lifeboat line.
zones.effect: These balconies jut out for wider side views without lifeboat obstruction below, sit low and central for steadier motion, and typically price lower than high-deck cabins despite the view advantage.
zones.mattersTo: Value play for anyone wanting balcony width and clear views without paying for upper decks; ideal for those prioritizing steady ride over height.

zones.what: Solarium pool, whirlpools, and outdoor seating directly above on Deck 14.
zones.effect: Expect noise from pool activity, chair scraping, and conversation overhead from morning through evening; some vibration from whirlpool pumps.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone in cabin during the day should avoid; doesn't matter if you're only there to sleep late at night.

zones.what: Two70 entertainment venue with robotic screens and performance space directly above on Deck 14.
zones.effect: Evening show noise, music, and audience activity overhead; typically quiet during daytime hours.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to early sleepers during show times; doesn't matter to night owls or those attending the shows anyway.

zones.what: Royal Theater spans Decks 3-5 directly below most of Deck 6.
zones.effect: Show music, audience movement, and stage effects audible in cabins during evening performances; typically two shows per night on sea days.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone wanting early-evening quiet or turning in before 10 PM; minimal impact if you attend the shows or stay out late.

zones.what: Music Hall live venue on Deck 6 directly below.
zones.effect: Live music and late-night entertainment noise from below, particularly during evening and night hours.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers should avoid; doesn't matter to those who enjoy the energy or are out late.

zones.what: SeaPlex activity space (sports court, bumper cars, roller skating) on Deck 10 aft, two to three decks below.
zones.effect: Intermittent activity noise and vibration from bumper cars and sports during daytime and early evening; typically quieter after 10 PM.
zones.mattersTo: Matters during sea days when SeaPlex is heavily used; less impact on port days or for those out of cabin during activity hours.

zones.what: Deck 13 aft features outdoor sports and activity areas directly overhead.
zones.effect: Daytime noise from sports activities, jogging track use, and outdoor games above.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to those in cabin during the day; minimal impact if you're exploring the ship or in port.

zones.what: Proximity to engine room below and propulsion systems creates low-frequency vibration in aft cabins, most noticeable on lower decks.
zones.effect: Subtle vibration and low hum at cruising speed; more noticeable during maneuvering and departure/arrival; Deck 6 aft typically feels it most.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to vibration-sensitive sleepers and those bothered by constant background hum; many guests don't notice or find it soothing.

zones.what: Bow thrusters and anchor machinery in forward sections create intermittent noise and vibration during docking and anchoring.
zones.effect: Loud mechanical noise and vibration during port arrivals, departures, and tendering operations; anchor chain noise every port morning.
zones.mattersTo: Critical for anyone who wants to sleep in on port days; doesn't matter to early risers or those prioritizing low price.

zones.what: Elevator banks located forward, mid-ship, and aft on all guest cabin decks with typical cruise ship positioning.
zones.effect: Cabins adjacent to elevator lobbies have convenient access but experience door chimes, conversation, and foot traffic at all hours; cabins mid-corridor trade some steps for quiet.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests benefit from elevator proximity; light sleepers should avoid cabins immediately adjacent to lobbies.
